Part 1

What must the controls achieve, and how does one loop work?

Part 1 · the plan

Why, how, and on what

  1. Six control objectivessafety first, then quality, equipment, environment, economics
  2. The feedback loopPV, SP, OP, error and the PID law
  3. Reverse or direct actingwhich way the output must move
  4. Classifying the variablescontrolled, manipulated, disturbance, monitored

Step 1 · objectives

Six objectives, in order of priority

ObjectiveIn this unitLoops that serve it
Safetyno overpressure, no coil burn-outEMS UY-105, PIC-102, FIC-105A/B
Product qualitynaphtha end point, diesel 90 %, AGO colourTIC-102, HIC-101/102, FIC-111/112
Equipmenttube metal, pump suction, floodingFIC-105A/B, LIC-107, LIC-108/109
Environmentno flaring, no oil in brinePIC-102 split range, LIC-103/161
Economicscharge with the least fuelFIC-114, FIC-104/108, TIC-101
Stable operationsmooth flows downstreamLIC-107 → FIC-1102, LIC-101 → FIC-100

Step 2 · one loop

Measure, compare, move the valve

$e$
error, SP − PV (reverse) or PV − SP (direct)
% span
$K_c,\ T_i,\ T_d$
gain, integral time, derivative time
%/%, s, s
$$OP = K_c\left[e + \frac{1}{T_i}\int e\,dt + T_d\frac{de}{dt}\right]$$

Step 3 · interactive · controller action

Which way must the output move?

proportional part$\Delta OP = K_c\,e$

A colder coil needs more fuel (reverse); a hotter top needs more reflux and a higher level more outflow (direct).

Step 4 · interactive · click a variable

Controlled, manipulated, disturbance or monitored?

Disturbances cannot be moved, only rejected; monitored variables stay in view through alarms, not loops.

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • Safety comes before quality, equipment, environment and economics.
  • A loop measures PV, compares it with SP and moves OP by the PID law.
  • The process gain sets the action: TIC-101 reverse, TIC-102 direct.

One loop is understood. Next: how many the unit needs, and how they are paired.

2

Part 2

How many loops does the unit need, and which valve moves which variable?

Part 2 · the plan

Count, pair, then connect

  1. Degrees of freedom29 independent final control elements
  2. Pairing rulesfast and direct, inventory in the direction of flow
  3. Control structurescascade, split range, manual selector

Step 1 · degrees of freedom

Count the valves that are free to movestep 1 of 2

$$N_{free} = N_{ctrl} - N_{slave} - N_{swing} + N_{bias}$$
$N_{ctrl} = 37$ controllers in the OTSevery loop on the DCS
$37 - 8 = 29$cascade slaves take their SP from a master
$29 - 1 + 1 = 29$swing fuel follows TIC-101; pass bias is free

Inventory 9 + throughput 1 leave 19 for quality, heat recovery and economics.

Interactive · click a group

Every free element has a jobstep 2 of 2

An extra controller would fight one already there; a missing one leaves a variable to drift.

Step 2 · pairing

Pair with the valve that acts soonest and moststep 1 of 2

  1. Fast, strong, directreflux moves the top temperature in seconds; fuel would take the whole tower
  2. Inventory in the direction of floweach level holds the flow that leaves its vessel; FIC-114 sets throughput once
  3. Cascade through a flow loopthe flow slave corrects pump and valve upsets first

Step 2 · pairing

Keep loops from fighting each otherstep 2 of 2

  1. Levels for averaginga level does not self-regulate; tune it to pass a smooth flow
  2. One automatic quality loopdraws HIC-101/102 stay in hand so TIC-102 is not fought
  3. Constraints in viewtube metal and flooding are watched by the pass loops and the EMS

Step 3 · interactive · split range

One output, three valves on V-4

direct actingpressure up → OP up

Gas is let in below 33 %, recycled below 67 %, flared only above 67 %: the flare is the last resort.

Step 3 · cascade

Eight masters set eight flow slaves

Master (slow)Slave (fast)What the slave absorbs
FIC-114 crude chargeFIC-105A, FIC-105Bpass hydraulics
TIC-101 COT (HS-101)FIC-106 fuel gasfuel header pressure
TIC-102 top temperatureFIC-101 refluxP-5 head
LIC-107, LIC-101FIC-1102 residue, FIC-100 naphthadownstream pressure
LIC-108, LIC-109, PIC-108FIC-102, FIC-113, FIC-129pump and valve changes

Structures are fixed. Next: how fast each loop should act.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • 29 free elements: 10 for inventory and throughput, 19 for the rest.
  • Pair fast and direct; hold levels with the outflow.
  • Cascades put a fast flow loop under each slow master.
  • PIC-102 lets gas in, recycles, and flares only last.
3

Part 3

How is a loop tested and tuned?

Part 3 · the plan

Test the process, then choose the speed

  1. P, PI or PIDwhat each mode adds and costs
  2. Step test and FOPDT fitgain, time constant and dead time from one step
  3. Lambda tuningKc and Ti from the model and a chosen speed
  4. Integrating levelstight or averaging, by the choice of λ

Step 1 · control modes

Integral removes offset; derivative helps slow, quiet loops

ModeStrengthWeaknessUsed here
Psimple, fastleaves an offsetpossible on averaging levels
PIremoves the offsetadds lag; short $T_i$ oscillatesall 34 PID loops
PIDfaster on lagging thermal loopsamplifies noisecandidate: TIC-101

Choosing the settings needs a model of the process. Next: a step test.

Step 2 · step test

Two points on the response give the modelstep 1 of 2

$K$
process gain, PV change per % output
%/%
$\tau,\ \theta$
time constant, dead time
s
$t_{28},\ t_{63}$
times to 28.3 % and 63.2 % of the final change
s
$$G(s) = \frac{K\,e^{-\theta s}}{\tau s+1}$$
$\tau = 1.5\,(t_{63}-t_{28}) = 1.5\,(150-78) = 108$ sTIC-101, +5 % fuel step
$\theta = t_{63} - \tau = 150 - 108 = 42$ stwo-point method

Interactive · step tests on the model

Self-regulating or integrating?step 2 of 2

Temperatures, flows and pressure settle (fit $K$, $\tau$, $\theta$); levels keep ramping, so the fit is a slope.

Step 3 · lambda tuning

Choose the speed, get the settingsstep 1 of 2

FOPDT$G(s) = K e^{-\theta s}/(\tau s+1)$
$$K_c = \frac{\tau}{|K|\,(\lambda+\theta)}, \qquad T_i = \tau$$
$K_c = \dfrac{108}{0.678\,(108+42)} = 1.06$ %/%TIC-101 with λ = τ

$K$ here is in % of the 200 °C span per % output; the OTS runs $K_c$ 1.2, $T_i$ 100 s.

Interactive · tuning lab, TIC-101

Too slow, about right, or oscillating?step 2 of 2

PI law$OP = K_c\,[e + \tfrac{1}{T_i}\int e\,dt]$

+5 °C set-point step on the fitted FOPDT; grey is the full simulator with the OTS tuning, so the model can be checked.

Step 4 · interactive · LIC-107

A level loop chooses what it passes downstream

integrating λ$T_i = 2\lambda+\theta,\ K_c = \dfrac{T_i}{|K_p|(\lambda+\theta)^2}$

A 5 % jump in the bottoms inflow: a short λ holds the level and slams the vacuum unit; a long λ lets the level absorb it.

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • A step test gives $K$, $\tau$, $\theta$: TIC-101 is 0.68 %/%, 108 s, 42 s.
  • Lambda tuning turns the model and a chosen speed into $K_c$ and $T_i$.
  • Levels integrate; λ decides between tight and averaging.

To keep

Key Takeaways

1

Rank the objectives first; safety loops are never traded for quality.

2

Count the free valves, then give each one exactly one job.

3

Put a fast flow slave under every slow master.

4

Step-test before tuning, and pick λ for what downstream needs.
